about: Which checks of tools/test.sh cover a file: what `tools/test.sh changed` runs for the files
changed. The first rule whose pattern matches a path decides (fnmatch on the path from the
repository's root, where * also matches /). "plugin" is the plugin-check of the plugin whose
folder the path is in; "self" is the changed test module of tests/vpair itself, with every
module that imports it. A path no rule names is reported, and the levels cover it.
The rules are narrow on purpose, and the levels (tools/test.sh all, before every push) cover
what they leave out. A plugin's editor-only files (its EDITOR sources, and the headers that
only they include, or that other sources include only where SPEAKER_HEADLESS is 0) run the
plugin's own check, not chain. The chain's modules run the headless builds, which never compile
them, and one complete build, loudness's, whose identity plugin_identity reads: `plugin <name>`
builds that bundle too, editor and all, and checks its identity. A speakerd file runs
`speakerd` and, beside it, only the checks whose scenarios alone read what the file is for: its
log lines, its answers on the command line or the local link, the values it streams, the
PipeWire objects it makes. The map is keyed by the file edited: an edit runs its own rule's
checks and no other's. One rule is narrower than that, on purpose: Engine.* runs
`speakerd` alone, though parts of the Engine are proven only by pair, chain and installers (its
rule says which); the levels run those before a push, and its "by_hand" says what to run
after touching those parts. A rule's optional "by_hand" is such advice: tools/impact.py, and
so `tools/test.sh changed`, says it on stderr, once, when files the rule decides changed.
The build tools run the checks that build through them: tools/build.sh chain (and tools, whose
pool self-test reads its waiting line), tools/jobserver.sh plugins and chain, whose links an edit of
it does not redo (its by_hand does), and tools (test_jobserver.py); tools/container.sh and tools/schedule.py run tools, which runs
in the one and as a schedule of the other, and whose tests prove the schedule with stand-in steps.
tools/tests/test_impact.py keeps the map honest: every speakerd file is named by a rule of its
own, every path a plugin rule without chain names is editor-only, and every plugin has a rule
of its own: one that runs `plugin` when it lists TARGETS (plugin-check needs its three builds),
and otherwise one whose by_hand builds it (ampScope: no check builds it, `plugin <name>` cannot).

rules.why: words and drawings

a plugin's editor-only files: in its complete and control builds, never in the headless builds the chain runs; the one complete build the chain reads, loudness's identity in plugin_identity, `plugin <name>` builds too and checks
one plugin: its SOURCES, DSP, CMakeLists.txt and probes, which its headless build compiles

ampScope: it lists no TARGETS, so it builds only its complete target; plugin-check builds and checks the three builds of a plugin with TARGETS, the chain runs headless builds, the controller compiles control builds, and a speaker's bundle carries none of it. No check, and no level, builds it: its by_hand says what does
rules.by_hand: no check builds ampScope (it lists no TARGETS, so `plugin ampScope` cannot run plugin-check): build it, `tools/build.sh ampScope`

rules.why: how every plugin builds, ampScope included: SpeakerPlugin.cmake and SourceId.cmake, and the JUCE submodule. `plugins` and chain build only the plugins with TARGETS, so its by_hand builds ampScope
rules.by_hand: ampScope builds with this too and no check builds it: build it, `tools/build.sh ampScope`

rules.why: what every plugin shares

speakerd's audio cycle, which every speakerd scenario plays through. speakerd alone on purpose, although parts of the Engine are proven only by other checks: its parameter inbox (knob_latency, graph_edit, drag_during_revision, ampd_persistence: pair), its live graph swap in Engine::install (graph_edit, buffer_size: pair; plugin_identity: chain), its level ring (meter_values, monitor_fanout: pair; chain_cost's output/level: chain) and its timing ring (chain_cost: chain; board_cpu: pair; smoke's timing line in test_speakerd_installed: installers). The levels run those before a push; after touching those parts, run what by_hand says
rules.by_hand: after touching Engine's parameter inbox, Engine::install or its level and timing rings, run `tools/test.sh speakerd pair chain installers`

rules.why: speakerd's command line and start: --version (the installers refuse one below their minimum and keep its line), the flags the installed unit passes, the device and playing lines smoke reads, the exit on a signal the unit's wrapper records, a shadowed --lv2-bundle refused with status 2 (installers); its control timer, which calls control.service(), where every live revision applies (pair; plugin_identity's apply: chain), and control.notifyStatus(), the unasked status test_buffer_size reads (pair); and the monitor it wires to Control (pair, chain)

speakerd's build: its version, which --version says and the installers check against their minimum, and how every file of it compiles (flags, definitions, modules), so that an edit can break what pair reads or move chain_cost's CPU figures: every check that runs speakerd
the generated BuildInfo.h: the version and commit --version says, which the installers check and keep as the installed build
device.json: the speakerd scenarios read the limits line; only the installers' scenarios have speakerd read a device.json the installers wrote, and smoke matches that line exactly
the state layers: the speakerd scenarios read `using layer`; only the installers' unit passes --from, and its wrapper's scenario reads `starting at layer ... (--from)`

the PipeWire node: the sink, the links and the quantum the speakerd scenarios play through; the sink speakerd makes without the drop-in (`NO INPUT SINK CONFIGURED`) and the amplifier as the only driver, which the installers' scenarios check; clock.force-quantum, which only pair's buffer_size sets
the local link's socket: ampd's connection (pair, chain's clients alike); its default path and the busy answer, which only smoke's status meets

the local link's operations: ampd's (pair); the apply and the subscriptions the chain's modules make themselves, plugin_identity's apply of revision 2 (its `applied` line and the `plugin node` lines of the graph it builds, once each) and chain_cost's speakerd/timing and output/level (chain); and the status with its timing, which only smoke reads (installers)

the monitor thread: output/level and the plugins' streams (pair; chain_cost's output/level), speakerd/timing (chain_cost: chain; board_cpu: pair), and the timing lines in the log and the status's timing, which smoke parses (installers)

the timing statistics: speakerd/timing's values, which TimingStats::toVar builds (chain_cost asserts them: chain; board_cpu checks their shape: pair), the status's timing and the `timing: last <n> s` line (smoke: installers)

a plugin node and its time: every node runs through it (speakerd); its time per node, which chain_cost asserts (chain), board_cpu finds in speakerd/timing (node 16: pair) and smoke prints per node from speakerd's status, the line test_speakerd_installed asserts (installers)

which bundle each plugin runs from, read from ~/.lv2 and every --lv2-bundle at start, which test_speakerd_installed meets with a broken copy of the bundle in ~/.lv2 (installers), and its build identity in the `plugin node` lines, which only plugin_identity reads (chain)
the graph built from a document, which every speakerd scenario plays, and the `plugin node` line it writes for each plugin, which only plugin_identity reads
the graph document: every layer the speakerd scenarios load; its top-level quantum, which only pair's buffer_size gives
the offline render, which the speakerd scenarios compare the live sound with (its `plugin node` lines are GraphBuilder's)
the `speakerd: ` lines: every check reads them, the speakerd scenarios too

speakerd's DISPLAY, one no X server has, set first in main (Main.cpp) and in speakerd-make-filtergraph (examples/MakeFiltergraph.cpp): every speakerd scenario starts speakerd, and its plugins' message threads, after it, and speakerd_no_display (in the speakerd check) reads what it is for (README.md, "No X display"): neither connects to an Xvfb, DISPLAY naming it or unset, and speakerd plays on once it is killed. speakerd-make-filtergraph no check builds: its by_hand says how
rules.by_hand: speakerd-make-filtergraph, which sets it too, builds only on request, and no check builds it: `tools/container.sh cmake --build build/speakerd --target speakerd-make-filtergraph`

rules.why: speakerd alone: the import of an AudioPluginHost session (speakerd_import, with the examples), the plugins' LV2 state, the sample helpers
a speakerd file no rule above names: everything that runs speakerd, until it is named (tools/tests/test_impact.py fails meanwhile)
the controller
ampd
the installers, what they install around speakerd, and the board script
a test module of the virtual pair
a self-test of the virtual pair's tools (pool_selftest.py: the pool's failure paths), which the tools check runs
the virtual pair itself: every check that runs on it; and tools, which runs the self-tests of its tools (pool.py's)

the make jobserver every build's `cmake --build` runs under: tools/build.sh's (the pool's prebuild, which builds chain's speakerd and its headless plugins with LTO) and plugin-check's (its run.sh: each plugin's six targets with LTO, which `plugins` builds). `plugin <name>` builds without LTO, where the jobserver has nothing to share. tools runs tools/tests/test_jobserver.py: the command's exit status, the jobserver it serves (MAKEFLAGS, its descriptors, its tokens), the signals and locale as given, the fallbacks. An edit of it changes no build's inputs, so on trees that are up to date these checks run it around links with nothing to do: its by_hand says how to make them link
rules.by_hand: an edit of tools/jobserver.sh relinks nothing: make a link of each path draw its tokens, `touch dsp/juce_plugins/loudness/LoudnessDsp.cpp`, then `BPI_TEST_LTO=1 tools/test.sh plugin loudness chain` (plugin-check's six LTO links, the prebuild's loudness_headless) and `tools/build.sh loudness aarch64 headless` (the cross-compiler's, which only the unit level builds)

rules.why: how every application and plugin builds, its tree's lock and its copy into <tree>/copied/{lv2,vst3}: chain's prebuild builds both kinds of what it builds (speakerd, an application; loudness complete and the three headless plugins, with LTO) and plugin_identity reads their build identity; tools runs pool_selftest.py, which checks the line tools/build.sh says while it waits for its tree's lock against the one the pool passes through. The aarch64 build and its copy only the unit level checks (buildinfo-aarch64): its by_hand
rules.by_hand: only the unit level builds for aarch64 and checks the copy (buildinfo-aarch64): run what it runs, `tools/build.sh loudness aarch64 headless && tools/container.sh dsp/juce_plugins/tests/buildinfo/check.sh --arch aarch64 loudness build/aarch64/loudness/loudness_headless_artefacts/Release/LV2/loudness_headless.lv2 build/aarch64/loudness/copied/lv2/loudness_headless.lv2`

rules.why: the development container every script moves into (container_or_native), and ccache_env: `tools/test.sh tools`, the cheapest check, runs in it, so it finds the image by its Containerfile's hash (or builds it), starts this checkout's container and runs a script there. CI runs natively (BPI_CONTAINER=0). Its --status, --stop and --prune no check runs: its by_hand
rules.by_hand: no check runs tools/container.sh's --status or --prune: run `tools/container.sh --status` and `tools/container.sh --prune --dry-run`, and read what they list

rules.why: the test tools. tools/schedule.py runs every check and level of more than one job, and still runs tools alone, as tools/test.sh does: test_schedule.py proves its phases, slots, niceness, dependents, gate, output, lock and signals; test_test_sh.py runs tools/test.sh through it with stand-in steps (the plan test.sh writes, the results it reads back, what each level records); pool_selftest.py the pool's side of its gate; and `tools/test.sh tools` itself runs as a schedule of one step. What real steps add, the levels run before a push
